title: Connection String Input
summary: Masks a database URL's password and reads back the host, user and TLS mode the driver will actually use, so it doesn't fail or connect insecurely.
description: Masks the password when not editing, reads back user, host, database and TLS mode, and catches unencoded @ # / % in passwords, localhost in production, missing or weak sslmode, unknown libpq parameters, wrong-database ports, Redis/MongoDB without TLS and .env quoting.
catches: Unencoded @, #, / or % in the password, naming the host a strict parser would use
Missing, weak or misspelled sslmode, and sslrootcert=system with a weaker mode
localhost in production and a port that belongs to another database
redis:// and MongoDB URLs without TLS (including mongodb+srv with tls=false)
Quotes or KEY= pasted from a .env file
limits: Parses the URL text; it doesn't try to connect or check credentials
Covers PostgreSQL (libpq), MySQL, MongoDB and Redis URL forms; other drivers may parse differently
Masking is visual: the full password is still in the value you receive
a11y: Visible <label>; aria-invalid and aria-describedby to a role="status" summary
Readback is a section labelled by its heading
Copy-masked button announces "Copied" in an aria-live="polite" span
After a fix, focus moves to the next fix or back to the field
server: Keep connection strings in a secrets manager and enforce TLS on the database server itself.

sources.label: PostgreSQL libpq: connection strings and sslmode

rules.note: Informational. Checked libpq sslmode values (prefer is the default) and that sslrootcert=system requires verify-full. MongoDB, MySQL and Redis conventions were not re-checked.

stops: Database URL leaks or skips TLS
